citations.quote: I should mention that my husband has been coughing for some weeks. We have not found out whether it is connected with the flat or whether it is just a stubborn cold going round his office.
The bathroom ceiling has grey-green mould on it, which keeps coming back after we clean it, and there is a musty smell in the hallway that you notice as soon as you come in.
On top of that, we wake up to cold bedrooms most mornings; the boiler has an error light on almost every morning, and the radiators upstairs are only lukewarm by breakfast.
Since nobody agrees on the cause, an independent building expert has to inspect the flat; I have asked Domicil Plus to commission one, and they refused.

plan.because: Needed to establish the parties, property and tenancy terms.
Obtain the original notice showing the defects reported and when.
Establish whether and when the landlord received the defect report.
Document the visible defects, locations and observation dates.
Establish the landlord’s responses, proposed work and access arrangements.
The reported mould activates the moisture and temperature evidence branch.
The reported heating problem activates the service-report branch.
Coughing is reported; medical findings and any limits on attributing its cause remain relevant.
An independent inspection is reported as needed and the cause is disputed. Provide any existing report, or arrange an inspection if none exists.
The claim does not mention a rent deposit; the silence policy presumes that branch absent for planning.
This is optional under the process.

questions: Is there an immediate health or safety concern, including severe symptoms or inadequate heat? If so, seek prompt medical or emergency assistance as appropriate.
When did the defects begin, and when and how were they reported to the landlord?
Has a heating service or independent inspection already taken place, and are reports available?
What work or access arrangements has the landlord proposed, if any?
